BEFORE YOU LAUNCH

THE SHORT VERSION.

Every quiz has seven prompts and 25 seconds for one answer to each. You can pause an active solo prompt without losing its remaining time. Big Quiz rotates through the large archive; Daily Quiz repeats its smaller route for the day. Obvious answers take you a little higher. Unexpected answers take you a lot higher. When a correct answer crosses one or more ascent landmarks, each reached level gets its own checkpoint; press STILL FLYING to continue the journey. Clear spelling slips are corrected when the intended answer is unambiguous — but the answer still has to fit the prompt.

Big Quiz starts with a balanced seven-prompt mix of familiar questions and fair atlas facts from the 10,000-plus prompt archive. A rare deep-atlas pull only opens after a 500-point personal best. Daily Quiz repeats the same seven prompts for your local date from a smaller hand-picked pool. Every active prompt uses a fixed offline answer set; broad auto-generated word puzzles are not used. Clear typos are corrected only against the displayed prompt’s answers and only when one correction is unambiguous. If an answer does not fit a prompt, its hint explains the exact rule. Flight Log entries stay on this device and never include your answer text. Sound effects stay off unless you switch them on; switching on sends a three-note test signal, then valid answers that earn points fire the thrust SFX.

Your ship climbs through real spaceflight landmarks — from the stratosphere and the Challenger disaster to Laika, Ham, Yuri Gagarin, the Moon, and beyond.

Scores and rarity ratings are hand-estimated for this offline game, not based on live players. “IQ” labels are just for fun, not an IQ test. Distances are approximate, the journey is not to scale, and historical scenes are illustrations. UFOs are fiction. Rotating Earth map: NASA/GSFC Blue Marble.
